{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01S3ucftnHEwZy476WJwoTGH","type":"tool_result","content":"     1→# Axxess — Product Research\n     2→\n     3→Researched: 2026-02-15\n     4→Developer website: https://www.axxess.com\n     5→\n     6→## Overview\n     7→\n     8→Axxess Technology Solutions is a Dallas, TX-based healthcare technology company specializing in home-based care software. Founded in 2007 by John Olajide as a home healthcare consulting firm, Axxess pivoted to software in 2011 and has grown into a bootstrapped unicorn with approximately 1,000 employees. The company has not raised external venture funding. Axxess serves over 9,000 organizations, with more than 800,000 users, 7 million+ patients served, and $37 billion+ in claims processed. Its core market is home health agencies, hospice providers, home care organizations, and palliative care providers across the United States. The majority of its customers are small to mid-size agencies (20–49 employees).\n     9→\n    10→Axxess offers a suite of cloud-based products for healthcare-at-home: **Home Health**, **Home Care** (skilled and private-pay), **Hospice**, and **Palliative Care** software platforms, along with ancillary solutions including Revenue Cycle Management, CAHPS surveys, staffing (Axxess CARE), training/compliance (Certification+), data exchange (Axxess Exchange), business intelligence, and an AI platform (Axxess Intelligence). The company holds ACHC, HITRUST, ISO 9001, and CHAP certifications.\n    11→\n    12→## Product: Axxess Palliative\n    13→\n    14→CHPL IDs: 11620\n    15→\n    16→### What It Is\n    17→\n    18→Axxess Palliative is a cloud-based electronic health record and practice management system designed specifically for palliative care delivery. The vendor describes it as \"the first custom-built software solution designed specifically for the delivery of palliative care.\" It is a distinct product within the broader Axxess platform ecosystem, sharing integration points with Axxess' Revenue Cycle Management and other enterprise solutions but operating as its own certified product.\n    19→\n    20→The certified module covers clinical documentation, CPOE, demographics, transitions of care, clinical quality measures, FHIR APIs, and direct messaging — a broad set of 27 ONC criteria including (a)(1) CPOE, (a)(5) demographics, (a)(12) family health history, (a)(14) implantable device list, (b)(1) transitions of care, (c)(1-3) clinical quality measures, (g)(7)/(g)(10) FHIR/API, and (h)(1) direct project.\n    21→\n    22→The product targets physicians and nurse practitioners delivering palliative care services, typically in home-based settings. It is designed for outpatient/ambulatory palliative care as indicated by the CHPL SED description.\n    23→\n    24→### Users & Market\n    25→\n    26→Day-to-day users are physicians, nurse practitioners, clinical staff, and administrative/billing personnel at palliative care organizations. The product supports the unique workflow of palliative care — focused on symptom management, health goal planning, and quality of life rather than curative treatment.\n    27→\n    28→Given that Axxess serves 9,000+ organizations overall, the palliative care product represents a newer and smaller segment of their customer base. The palliative care product was certified in March 2025 (version 3.0.2022), suggesting it has been in market for several years. No specific customer counts for the palliative product alone were found. The broader Axxess platform is well-reviewed, with an 81% satisfaction rating across ~417 reviews on third-party sites, and 87% of reviewers recommending Axxess products to others.\n    29→\n    30→### Modules & Functionality\n    31→\n    32→Based on vendor materials, help center documentation, and the product's navigation structure, Axxess Palliative includes the following functional areas:\n    33→\n    34→**Intake/Scheduling**\n    35→- Patient intake workflows from referral through admission\n    36→- Patient scheduling with calendar and list views (14-day and monthly)\n    37→- Employee scheduling by branch, employment status, and team\n    38→- Color-coded task statuses (scheduled/completed/missed/pending)\n    39→- Bulk task creation and visit history tracking\n    40→- Filtering by branch, patient status (Active, Discharged, Pending, Non-Admitted, Deceased)\n    41→- Insurance eligibility checking within patient charts (per help center)\n    42→\n    43→**Clinical Documentation**\n    44→- Physician/NP-focused visit documentation\n    45→- Comprehensive Plan of Care management\n    46→- Patient demographics with banner display (name, MRN, age, code status, diagnosis, insurance)\n    47→- Medication profiles and electronic Medication Administration Records (eMAR)\n    48→- Allergy documentation\n    49→- Infectious disease tracking\n    50→- Diagnosis documentation\n    51→- Vital signs recording\n    52→- Symptom ratings/assessments\n    53→- Physician communications\n    54→- Advance directives\n    55→- Emergency preparedness documentation\n    56→- Implantable device list (per certification criteria)\n    57→- Family health history (per certification criteria)\n    58→- Medi-Span drug database integration for drug interaction checking\n    59→\n    60→**Orders Management**\n    61→- Medication orders (from medication profiles or clinical visits)\n    62→- DME (Durable Medical Equipment) orders\n    63→- Supply orders\n    64→- Other orders (e.g., discharge directives)\n    65→- Order creation from multiple pathways: patient/employee schedule, patient profile, medication profile, clinical visits\n    66→- Order read-back and verification workflow\n    67→- Prescribing provider auto-population and signature management\n    68→- Medication refill workflows with refill history tracking\n    69→- Orders   99→- Talk-to-text documentation\n   100→- Mobile scheduling\n   101→- Mobile orders management\n   102→- Mobile CPT code selection\n   103→\n   104→**Axxess Intelligence (AI)**\n   105→- AI-driven insurance/payer information, referral source, authorized contacts, emergency preparedness details, advance directives.\n   122→\n   123→**Clinical Records**: Visit notes, vital signs, symptom ratings/assessments, diagnoses (including primary and secondary), medication profiles with eMAR, allergies, infectious disease status, implantable device list, family health history, Comprehensive Plan of Care, physician communications/notes, order documentation (medications, DME, supplies).\n   124→\n   125→**Scheduling & Workflow Data**: Patient and employee schedules, task assignments and statuses, visit history, co-signature and addendum tracking.\n   126→\n   127→**IDG Meeting Records**: Meeting schedules, agendas, summaries, sign-in sheets, team member assignments, patient review documentation.\n   128→\n   129→**Billing & Financial Data**: Medicare Part B claims, multi-payer claims, CPT codes, ERA data, insurance eligibility records, billing calculations. The revenue cycle management integration suggests claims data and payment information flow through the system.\n   130→\n   131→**Administrative Data**: Employee/staff profiles, branch assignments, team structures, pharmacy and DME vendor information, referral records.\n   132→\n   133→**Audit & Compliance Data**: Per certification criteria (d)(1-9), the system maintains audit logs, authentication records, and security-related data.\n   134→\n   135→The website does not explicitly mention patient portal/patient-facing access (no (e)(1) certification), and there is no mention of e-prescribing (no (a)(2) certification). Public health reporting beyond clinical quality measures is not certified. Founded in 2007 by John Olajide as a home healthcare consulting firm, Axxess pivoted to software in 2011 and has grown into a bootstrapped unicorn with approximately 1,000 employees. The company has not raised external venture funding. Axxess serves over 9,000 organizations, with more than 800,000 users, 7 million+ patients served, and $37 billion+ in claims processed. Its core market is home health agencies, hospice providers, home care organizations, and palliative care providers across the United States. The majority of its customers are small to mid-size agencies (20–49 employees).\n\nAxxess offers a suite of cloud-based products for healthcare-at-home: **Home Health**, **Home Care** (skilled and private-pay), **Hospice**, and **Palliative Care** software platforms, along with ancillary solutions including Revenue Cycle Management, CAHPS surveys, staffing (Axxess CARE), training/compliance (Certification+), data exchange (Axxess Exchange), business intelligence, and an AI platform (Axxess Intelligence). The company holds ACHC, HITRUST, ISO 9001, and CHAP certifications.\n\n## Product: Axxess Palliative\n\nCHPL IDs: 11620\n\n### What It Is\n\nAxxess Palliative is a cloud-based electronic health record and practice management system designed specifically for palliative care delivery. The vendor describes it as \"the first custom-built software solution designed specifically for the delivery of palliative care.\" It is a distinct product within the broader Axxess platform ecosystem, sharing integration points with Axxess' Revenue Cycle Management and other enterprise solutions but operating as its own certified product.\n\nThe certified module covers clinical documentation, CPOE, demographics, transitions of care, clinical quality measures, FHIR APIs, and direct messaging — a broad set of 27 ONC criteria including (a)(1) CPOE, (a)(5) demographics, (a)(12) family health history, (a)(14) implantable device list, (b)(1) transitions of care, (c)(1-3) clinical quality measures, (g)(7)/(g)(10) FHIR/API, and (h)(1) direct project.\n\nThe product targets physicians and nurse practitioners delivering palliative care services, typically in home-based settings. It is designed for outpatient/ambulatory palliative care as indicated by the CHPL SED description.\n\n### Users & Market\n\nDay-to-day users are physicians, nurse practitioners, clinical staff, and administrative/billing personnel at palliative care organizations. The product supports the unique workflow of palliative care — focused on symptom management, health goal planning, and quality of life rather than curative treatment.\n\nGiven that Axxess serves 9,000+ organizations overall, the palliative care product represents a newer and smaller segment of their customer base. The palliative care product was certified in March 2025 (version 3.0.2022), suggesting it has been in market for several years. No specific customer counts for the palliative product alone were found. The broader Axxess platform is well-reviewed, with an 81% satisfaction rating across ~417 reviews on third-party sites, and 87% of reviewers recommending Axxess products to others.\n\n### Modules & Functionality\n\nBased on vendor materials, help center documentation, and the product's navigation structure, Axxess Palliative includes the following functional areas:\n\n**Intake/Scheduling**\n- Patient intake workflows from referral through admission\n- Patient scheduling with calendar and list views (14-day and monthly)\n- Employee scheduling by branch, employment status, and team\n- Color-coded task statuses (scheduled/completed/missed/pending)\n- Bulk task creation and visit history tracking\n- Filtering by branch, patient status (Active, Discharged, Pending, Non-Admitted, Deceased)\n- Insurance eligibility checking within patient charts (per help center)\n\n**Clinical Documentation**\n- Physician/NP-focused visit documentation\n- Comprehensive Plan of Care management\n- Patient demographics with banner display (name, MRN, age, code status, diagnosis, insurance)\n- Medication profiles and electronic Medication Administration Records (eMAR)\n- Allergy documentation\n- Infectious disease tracking\n- Diagnosis documentation\n- Vital signs recording\n- Symptom ratings/assessments\n- Physician communications\n- Advance directives\n- Emergency preparedness documentation\n- Implantable device list (per certification criteria)\n- Family health history (per certification criteria)\n- Medi-Span drug database integration for drug interaction checking\n\n**Orders Management**\n- Medication orders (from medication profiles or clinical visits)\n- DME (Durable Medical Equipment) orders\n- Supply orders\n- Other orders (e.g., discharge directives)\n- Order creation from multiple pathways: patient/employee schedule, patient profile, medication profile, clinical visits\n- Order read-back and verification workflow\n- Prescribing provider auto-population and signature management\n- Medication refill workflows with refill history tracking\n- Orders flow to Comprehensive Plan of Care and IDG assessments\n\n**IDG (Interdisciplinary Group) Center**\n- IDG meeting scheduling and management\n- Automated agenda and summary generation\n- IDG Prep Report for clinical document verification\n- Patient categorization by status (admission, active, discharge, death)\n- Meeting history with agendas and sign-in sheets\n- Team member and group management\n- Hospice physician assignments\n- Patient rosters prioritized by recertification urgency\n\n**Billing**\n- Direct Medicare Part B billing through Axxess' Network Service Vendor connection to Medicare\n- Multi-payer billing through integration with Axxess Revenue Cycle Management\n- Claims submission automation\n- CPT code selection (including mobile CPT code selector with AI-assisted selection via Axxess Intelligence)\n- Electronic Remittance Advice (ERA) processing\n- Billing calculators\n\n**Administration**\n- Administrator dashboard\n- Authorized contacts management\n- Referral tracking\n- Payer/insurance information management\n- Pharmacy and DME vendor management\n\n**Mobile**\n- iOS and Android mobile apps\n- Offline visit documentation with sync\n- Talk-to-text documentation\n- Mobile scheduling\n- Mobile orders management\n- Mobile CPT code selection\n\n**Axxess Intelligence (AI)**\n- AI-driven CPT code suggestion on mobile\n- Other AI capabilities (details limited on the palliative-specific pages)\n\n**Integrations**\n- Axxess Revenue Cycle Management integration\n- Axxess Exchange (secure data exchange)\n- Medicare Network Service Vendor direct connection\n- Medi-Span drug database\n- Direct messaging (per h(1) certification)\n- FHIR API (per g(10) certification)\n- 40+ interoperable integrations noted for the broader Axxess platform\n\n### Data & Content\n\nBased on the features and help documentation, Axxess Palliative stores and manages the following data:\n\n**Patient Data**: Demographics, contact information, addresses, MRN, age, code status, insurance/payer information, referral source, authorized contacts, emergency preparedness details, advance directives.\n\n**Clinical Records**: Visit notes, vital signs, symptom ratings/assessments, diagnoses (including primary and secondary), medication profiles with eMAR, allergies, infectious disease status, implantable device list, family health history, Comprehensive Plan of Care, physician communications/notes, order documentation (medications, DME, supplies).\n\n**Scheduling & Workflow Data**: Patient and employee schedules, task assignments and statuses, visit history, co-signature and addendum tracking.\n\n**IDG Meeting Records**: Meeting schedules, agendas, summaries, sign-in sheets, team member assignments, patient review documentation.\n\n**Billing & Financial Data**: Medicare Part B claims, multi-payer claims, CPT codes, ERA data, insurance eligibility records, billing calculations. The revenue cycle management integration suggests claims data and payment information flow through the system.\n\n**Administrative Data**: Employee/staff profiles, branch assignments, team structures, pharmacy and DME vendor information, referral records.\n\n**Audit & Compliance Data**: Per certification criteria (d)(1-9), the system maintains audit logs, authentication records, and security-related data.\n\nThe website does not explicitly mention patient portal/patient-facing access (no (e)(1) certification), and there is no mention of e-prescribing (no (a)(2) certification). Public health reporting beyond clinical quality measures is not certified. The product does not appear to include lab ordering or results management based on the absence of those certification criteria.\n\n---\n","numLines":138,"startLine":1,"totalLines":138}}}

Starting Point: From the main navigation, select the 'Patients' and then\nthe 'Download Patient Chart' option.\n2. Choose your parameters: Here, you can specify various parameters\nsuch as the Branch, date range, patient(s), and desired file format.\n3. Request: Initiate the export process by clicking 'Request Documents'.\nYour request will then enter a queue.\n4. Download: Once your export is ready and shows a 'Ready' status, click\n'Export' to download a zip file containing the requested data. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01NCrfhTnHysjfVi61iUr1Nz","type":"tool_result","content":"Costs or Fees\n\nCapability\n\nDescription of Capability\n\n§ 170.315(a)(1)\nComputerized Provider\nOrder Entry (CPOE) Medications\n\nAxxess Palliative enables a user to record, change, and access\nmedication orders.\n\n§ 170.315(a)(5)\nPatient demographics\nand observations\n\nAxxess Palliative enables a user to record, change, and access\npatient demographic and observations data including race,\nethnicity, preferred language, sex, sex parameter for clinical\nuse, sexual orientation, gender identity, name to use, pronouns\nand date of birth.\n\n§ 170.315(a)(12)\nFamily Health History\n\nAxxess Palliative enables a user to record, change, and access\na patient's family health history in accordance with the familial\nconcepts.\n\n§ 170.315(a)(14)\nImplantable Devices\n\nAxxess Palliative enables a user to record Unique Device\nIdentifiers associated with a patient's Implantable Devices.\n\n§ 170.315(b)(1)\nTransition of Care\n\nAxxess Palliative enables a user to create a transition of\ncare/referral summary formatted in accordance using the\nContinuity of Care Document, Referral Note, Discharge\nSummary document templates\n\n§ 170.315(b)(10)\nElectronic Health\nInformation Export\n\nAxxess Palliative enables a user to timely create an export\nfile(s) with all of a single patient’s or population of patient’s\nelectronic health information that can be stored.\n\n§ 170.315(b)(11)\nDecision Support\nInterventions\n\nAxxess Palliative enables a limited set of identified users to\nselect (i.e., activate) electronic decision support interventions.\n\n§ 170.315(d)(1)\nAuthentication, Access\nControl, Authorization\n\nAxxess Palliative enables unique user identification and\nauthentication against unique identifiers\n(e.g., username/password) before providing access to\nelectronic health information and includes the ability to control\nthe specific access and privilege rights a user is granted.\n\n§ 170.315(d)(2) Auditable\nEvents and TamperResistance\n\nAxxess Palliative supports auditable events for security auditing\nof access to electronic health information according to\nstandard.\n\n§ 170.315(d)(3) Audit\nReport(s)\n\nAuthorized users can create an audit report for a specific time\nperiod and can sort the entries in the\naudit log.\n\n§ 170.315(d)(4)\nAmendments\n\nAuthorized users can document patient requests for\namendments when the amendment is\naccepted and when denied.\n\nTypes of costs or fees that a user\nmay be required to pay to\npurchase, license, implement,\nmaintain, upgrade, use, or\notherwise enable and support the\nuse of the implementation or use of\nthe capability OR- in connection\nwith the data generated in the\ncourse using the capability\n\nAll costs are included within software\nlicenses fees according to contract\nterms and conditions\n\n\fCosts or Fees\n\nCapability\n\nDescription of Capability\n\n§ 170.315(d)(5)\nAutomatic Access Timeout\n\nAxxess Palliative automatically stops a user’s access after a\nperiod of inactivity and requires re-entry of credentials\naccording to regulatory guidance.\n\n§ 170.315(d)(6)\nEmergency Access\n\nAxxess Palliative has an emergency plan that can enable\nemergency access per emergency\npreparedness guidelines.\n\n§ 170.315(d)(7) End-user\nDevice Encryption\n\nAll data is stored in an encrypted format when application is not\nin use. Axxess Palliative encrypts data in alignment with\nregulatory standards.\n\n§ 170.315 (d)(8) Integrity\n\nAxxess Palliative leverages a hashing algorithm in alignment\nwith regulatory requirements.\n\n§170.315(d)(9) Trusted\nConnection\n§170.315(d)(12) Encrypt\nauthentication credentials\n\nAxxess Palliative encrypts stored authentication credentials.\n\n§170.315(d)(13) MultiFactor authentication\n\nAxxess Palliative supports the authentication, through multiple\nelements, of the user’s identity with the use of industryrecognized standards.\n\n§170.315(g)(3)\nSafety Enhanced {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_01AQeUBeHRgUrxSuFLiuAp65","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01GbBji4VdaRsAqwDheLpKYh","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/axxess--axxess-palliative/ehi-export-report.md","content":"# Axxess — EHI Export Documentation (Axxess Palliative)\n\nCollected: 2026-02-15\n\n## Source\n- Registered URL: https://www.axxess.com/cehrt/\n- CHPL IDs: 11620\n- Product: Axxess Palliative, Version 3.0.2022\n- Certification date: 2025-03-13\n\n## Navigation Journal\n\n1. **Initial probe** — `curl -sI -L \"https://www.axxess.com/cehrt/\"` returned HTTP 200, Content-Type: text/html, served by nginx/PHP. No redirects.\n\n2. **Page fetch and examination** — `curl -sL \"https://www.axxess.com/cehrt/\" -o /tmp/page.html` returned a 165KB HTML page titled \"CEHRT | Axxess\". The page is a static compliance/certification hub with a \"What is CEHRT?\" heading and two columns of document links.\n\n3. **Document links found** — Searched for downloadable files:\n   ```\n   grep -oiE 'href=\"[^\"]*\\.(pdf|zip|xlsx|csv|json)[^\"]*\"' /tmp/page.html\n   ```\n   Relevant results:\n   - `/assets/pdf/b10-electronic-health-information-export.pdf` — **Primary EHI export document**\n   - `/assets/pdf/Axxess-CEHRT-Disclosures-V3.0.2022.pdf` — CEHRT disclosures (includes b(10) capability description)\n   - `/assets/pdf/Compliance-Certificate-Axxess-Palliative-Version-3.0.2022-040825.pdf` — Compliance certificate (not downloaded; not technical)\n   - Real-World Testing Plans/Reports for 2024 and 2025 (not downloaded; not EHI export docs)\n\n4. **Downloaded the b10 PDF**:\n   ```bash\n   curl -sL \"https://www.axxess.com/assets/pdf/b10-electronic-health-information-export.pdf\" -o downloads/b10-electronic-health-information-export.pdf\n   ```\n   Verified: `file` confirms PDF document, version 1.6, 148,257 bytes, 1 page.\n\n5. **Downloaded the CEHRT Disclosures PDF**:\n   ```bash\n   curl -sL \"https://www.axxess.com/assets/pdf/Axxess-CEHRT-Disclosures-V3.0.2022.pdf\" -o downloads/Axxess-CEHRT-Disclosures-V3.0.2022.pdf\n   ```\n   Verified: PDF document, version 1.7, 3 pages, 210,127 bytes.\n\n6. **Checked for additional documentation** — Searched the CEHRT page for links to FHIR API docs, help pages, and other potential EHI export resources:\n   - `https://engage.axxess.com/api.html` — Partner API specifications (marketing/lead-gen page, not EHI export)\n   - `https://fhirpresentationdev.axxessweb.com/fhir/r4/endpoints` — FHIR endpoint listing (g)(10), not (b)(10)\n   - `https://r4dev.dynamicfhirsandbox.com/dhit/practicetwo/r4/Home/ApiDocumentation` — FHIR API sandbox docs (timed out; irrelevant to b(10))\n   - `https://www.axxess.com/help/axxess-palliative-care/` — Help center with ~40+ articles covering clinical, billing, admin features. No article specifically about \"Download Patient Chart\" or EHI export was found in the listing.\n\n7. **Took full-page screenshot** of the CEHRT page using browser automation.\n\n8. **Examined b10 PDF content** — Used `pdftotext` to extract text. The entire document is a single page with overview, file formats, and export process instructions. No embedded URLs, no attachments. Notable: the closing sentence reads \"This should comply with what we need and buy us time to finish the feature in the overall direction we are thinking\" — an internal note that was apparently left in the public-facing document.\n\n9. **Examined CEHRT Disclosures PDF** — 3-page document listing all certified criteria with brief descriptions. The (b)(10) entry states: \"Axxess Palliative enables a user to timely create an export file(s) with all of a single patient's or population of patient's electronic health information that can be stored.\" No additional technical detail.\n\n## What Was Found\n\nThe EHI export documentation consists of a **single 1-page PDF** (`b10-electronic-health-information-export.pdf`) that provides a brief overview of the export functionality. Here is the entirety of the substantive content:\n\n**Export Format:**\n- **XML**: Patient data conforming to C-CDA version 2.1 specification\n- **PDF**: Rendered patient documents\n\n**Export Mechanism:**\n- Navigate to Patients → Download Patient Chart\n- Select Branch, date range, patient(s), and desired file format\n- Click \"Request Documents\" (enters a processing queue)\n- When status shows \"Ready\", click \"Export\" to download a ZIP file\n- Each patient's data is organized in individual ZIP folders labeled `LASTNAME_FIRSTNAME`\n\n**Scope:** Single patient or population (multiple patients)\n\n**No data dictionary is provided.** There is no documentation of:\n- What specific data elements are included in the C-CDA export\n- Which C-CDA sections/templates are populated\n- Whether the export covers data beyond standard C-CDA sections\n- How billing data, palliative-care-specific assessments, or specialty clinical data are represented\n- Sample export files or example output\n- Any schema or machine-readable format specification beyond \"C-CDA 2.1\"\n\nThe internal-sounding closing sentence — \"This should comply with what we need and buy us time to finish the feature in the overall direction we are thinking\" — suggests this documentation was drafted as an interim compliance artifact rather than a thorough technical specification.\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nAxxess Palliative stores a rich set of data as documented in the product research: patient demographics, clinical visit notes, vital signs, symptom assessments, diagnoses, medications (with eMAR), allergies, infectious disease tracking, implantable devices, family health history, advance directives, comprehensive plan of care, physician communications, orders (medications, DME, supplies), IDG meeting records, Medicare Part B billing/claims, CPT codes, ERA data, payroll, insurance eligibility, and more.\n\nThe export documentation provides **no specifics whatsoever** about which data domains are included. It states only that the export produces \"comprehensive patient data\" in C-CDA 2.1 format.\n\n**Critical concern: C-CDA 2.1 is structurally insufficient for \"all electronic health information.\"** C-CDA is designed for clinical summary exchange (transitions of care, discharge summaries, referral notes). It has standardized sections for:\n- Demographics, problems, medications, allergies, procedures, results, vital signs, immunizations, plan of care, social history, encounters, functional status\n\nIt does **not** have standard sections for:\n- **Billing records** (claims, CPT codes, ERA data, payer information, financial transactions)\n- **Palliative care-specific assessments** (symptom ratings, IDG meeting documentation, comprehensive plan of care details)\n- **Orders management** (DME orders, supply orders, order workflows)\n- **Scheduling data** (though this is borderline EHI)\n- **Payroll and financial data** related to patient billing\n\nThis means the C-CDA export likely covers only the clinical summary slice of the patient record — analogous to a (b)(1) Transition of Care export — and misses significant portions of the designated record set. Without a data dictionary or detailed documentation, it's impossible to confirm, but the choice of C-CDA 2.1 as the sole structured format strongly suggests this is a (g)(10)-adjacent clinical summary, not a true (b)(10) \"all EHI\" export.\n\nThe alternative PDF format likely captures rendered versions of documents and notes, which could theoretically include more data, but PDFs are not computable and there's no documentation of what the PDF export contains.\n\n**Domains likely covered** (by virtue of C-CDA 2.1):\n- Demographics\n- Diagnoses/problems\n- Medications\n- Allergies\n- Vital signs\n- Immunizations\n- Procedures\n- Lab/diagnostic results (if applicable)\n- Encounters\n- Clinical notes (as unstructured text in C-CDA sections)\n\n**Domains likely missing or unverifiable:**\n- Billing records (claims, charges, payments, CPT codes, ERA)\n- Insurance/payer details\n- Palliative-specific clinical assessments and symptom ratings\n- IDG meeting records and documentation\n- Orders (DME, supplies)\n- Comprehensive plan of care (palliative-specific detail beyond C-CDA's generic plan of care section)\n- Advance directives (may be partially in C-CDA)\n- Physician communications\n- Emergency preparedness documentation\n- Referral tracking data\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\n- **Format**: C-CDA 2.1 XML and PDF, delivered in a ZIP archive\n- **Standard**: C-CDA (Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture) version 2.1 is a recognized HL7 standard for clinical document exchange\n- **Appropriateness**: C-CDA is appropriate for clinical summaries but is a poor fit for exporting \"all electronic health information\" from a palliative care EHR. A palliative care product stores specialty-specific data (symptom assessments, IDG records, comprehensive plans of care, billing) that doesn't map to C-CDA sections.\n- **Reconstruction**: A third party could reconstruct a basic clinical summary from the C-CDA export but almost certainly could not reconstruct the full patient record, especially billing, palliative-specific assessments, and administrative data.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\nThe documentation quality is **extremely poor**:\n- A single page with no technical depth\n- No data dictionary at all\n- No field-level definitions\n- No data types, value sets, or constraints\n- No sample exports or worked examples\n- No schema files or machine-readable specifications\n- No description of which C-CDA templates or sections are used\n- Contains an internal note (\"This should comply with what we need and buy us time to finish the feature\") that was not removed before publication\n- The documentation reads as an internal memo rather than a technical specification\n\nA developer could not implement an import of this data based on this documentation alone. They would know only that the export is \"C-CDA 2.1 XML\" in a ZIP — they'd need to reverse-engineer the actual structure from sample exports.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Granularity**: Zero field-level documentation. Not even table-level or section-level documentation.\n- **Value sets**: Not documented\n- **Relationships**: Not documented\n- **Versioning**: The PDF was created December 15, 2023. No change history.\n- **Machine-readable artifacts**: None provided\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://www.axxess.com/cehrt/\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no (all content accessible via curl)\n- Navigation complexity: one_click (PDF linked directly from CEHRT page)\n- Anti-bot issues: none\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- The FHIR API sandbox documentation (`r4dev.dynamicfhirsandbox.com`) timed out but was determined to be (g)(10) documentation, not relevant to the (b)(10) export.\n- The partner API page (`engage.axxess.com/api.html`) is a marketing/lead-gen page, not technical documentation.\n- The help center (`axxess.com/help/axxess-palliative-care/`) has ~40+ articles but none specifically about the \"Download Patient Chart\" EHI export feature. This is a gap — users have no publicly accessible guide for performing the export.\n- No enrichment was performed because the documentation corpus consists of only two PDFs (one 1-page, one 3-page) with no structured data to extract.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":240,"cache_read_input_tokens":53732,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":240},"output_tokens":25,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"0db1f87a-d6c8-4405-9216-8d092fd1540b","uuid":"ca88cff2-b87d-4dee-99c0-a5b51e30acdd"}

No redirects.\n\n2. **Page fetch and examination** — `curl -sL \"https://www.axxess.com/cehrt/\" -o /tmp/page.html` returned a 165KB HTML page titled \"CEHRT | Axxess\". The page is a static compliance/certification hub with a \"What is CEHRT?\" heading and two columns of document links.\n\n3. **Document links found** — Searched for downloadable files:\n   ```\n   grep -oiE 'href=\"[^\"]*\\.(pdf|zip|xlsx|csv|json)[^\"]*\"' /tmp/page.html\n   ```\n   Relevant results:\n   - `/assets/pdf/b10-electronic-health-information-export.pdf` — **Primary EHI export document**\n   - `/assets/pdf/Axxess-CEHRT-Disclosures-V3.0.2022.pdf` — CEHRT disclosures (includes b(10) capability description)\n   - `/assets/pdf/Compliance-Certificate-Axxess-Palliative-Version-3.0.2022-040825.pdf` — Compliance certificate (not downloaded; not technical)\n   - Real-World Testing Plans/Reports for 2024 and 2025 (not downloaded; not EHI export docs)\n\n4. **Downloaded the b10 PDF**:\n   ```bash\n   curl -sL \"https://www.axxess.com/assets/pdf/b10-electronic-health-information-export.pdf\" -o downloads/b10-electronic-health-information-export.pdf\n   ```\n   Verified: `file` confirms PDF document, version 1.6, 148,257 bytes, 1 page.\n\n5. **Downloaded the CEHRT Disclosures PDF**:\n   ```bash\n   curl -sL \"https://www.axxess.com/assets/pdf/Axxess-CEHRT-Disclosures-V3.0.2022.pdf\" -o downloads/Axxess-CEHRT-Disclosures-V3.0.2022.pdf\n   ```\n   Verified: PDF document, version 1.7, 3 pages, 210,127 bytes.\n\n6. **Checked for additional documentation** — Searched the CEHRT page for links to FHIR API docs, help pages, and other potential EHI export resources:\n   - `https://engage.axxess.com/api.html` — Partner API specifications (marketing/lead-gen page, not EHI export)\n   - `https://fhirpresentationdev.axxessweb.com/fhir/r4/endpoints` — FHIR endpoint listing (g)(10), not (b)(10)\n   - `https://r4dev.dynamicfhirsandbox.com/dhit/practicetwo/r4/Home/ApiDocumentation` — FHIR API sandbox docs (timed out; irrelevant to b(10))\n   - `https://www.axxess.com/help/axxess-palliative-care/` — Help center with ~40+ articles covering clinical, billing, admin features. No article specifically about \"Download Patient Chart\" or EHI export was found in the listing.\n\n7. **Took full-page screenshot** of the CEHRT page using browser automation.\n\n8. **Examined b10 PDF content** — Used `pdftotext` to extract text. The entire document is a single page with overview, file formats, and export process instructions. No embedded URLs, no attachments. Notable: the closing sentence reads \"This should comply with what we need and buy us time to finish the feature in the overall direction we are thinking\" — an internal note that was apparently left in the public-facing document.\n\n9. **Examined CEHRT Disclosures PDF** — 3-page document listing all certified criteria with brief descriptions. The (b)(10) entry states: \"Axxess Palliative enables a user to timely create an export file(s) with all of a single patient's or population of patient's electronic health information that can be stored.\" No additional technical detail.\n\n## What Was Found\n\nThe EHI export documentation consists of a **single 1-page PDF** (`b10-electronic-health-information-export.pdf`) that provides a brief overview of the export functionality. Here is the entirety of the substantive content:\n\n**Export Format:**\n- **XML**: Patient data conforming to C-CDA version 2.1 specification\n- **PDF**: Rendered patient documents\n\n**Export Mechanism:**\n- Navigate to Patients → Download Patient Chart\n- Select Branch, date range, patient(s), and desired file format\n- Click \"Request Documents\" (enters a processing queue)\n- When status shows \"Ready\", click \"Export\" to download a ZIP file\n- Each patient's data is organized in individual ZIP folders labeled `LASTNAME_FIRSTNAME`\n\n**Scope:** Single patient or population (multiple patients)\n\n**No data dictionary is provided.** There is no documentation of:\n- What specific data elements are included in the C-CDA export\n- Which C-CDA sections/templates are populated\n- Whether the export covers data beyond standard C-CDA sections\n- How billing data, palliative-care-specific assessments, or specialty clinical data are represented\n- Sample export files or example output\n- Any schema or machine-readable format specification beyond \"C-CDA 2.1\"\n\nThe internal-sounding closing sentence — \"This should comply with what we need and buy us time to finish the feature in the overall direction we are thinking\" — suggests this documentation was drafted as an interim compliance artifact rather than a thorough technical specification.\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nAxxess Palliative stores a rich set of data as documented in the product research: patient demographics, clinical visit notes, vital signs, symptom assessments, diagnoses, medications (with eMAR), allergies, infectious disease tracking, implantable devices, family health history, advance directives, comprehensive plan of care, physician communications, orders (medications, DME, supplies), IDG meeting records, Medicare Part B billing/claims, CPT codes, ERA data, payroll, insurance eligibility, and more.\n\nThe export documentation provides **no specifics whatsoever** about which data domains are included. It states only that the export produces \"comprehensive patient data\" in C-CDA 2.1 format.\n\n**Critical concern: C-CDA 2.1 is structurally insufficient for \"all electronic health information.\"** C-CDA is designed for clinical summary exchange (transitions of care, discharge summaries, referral notes). It has standardized sections for:\n- Demographics, problems, medications, allergies, procedures, results, vital signs, immunizations, plan of care, social history, encounters, functional status\n\nIt does **not** have standard sections for:\n- **Billing records** (claims, CPT codes, ERA data, payer information, financial transactions)\n- **Palliative care-specific assessments** (symptom ratings, IDG meeting documentation, comprehensive plan of care details)\n- **Orders management** (DME orders, supply orders, order workflows)\n- **Scheduling data** (though this is borderline EHI)\n- **Payroll and financial data** related to patient billing\n\nThis means the C-CDA export likely covers only the clinical summary slice of the patient record — analogous to a (b)(1) Transition of Care export — and misses significant portions of the designated record set. Without a data dictionary or detailed documentation, it's impossible to confirm, but the choice of C-CDA 2.1 as the sole structured format strongly suggests this is a (g)(10)-adjacent clinical summary, not a true (b)(10) \"all EHI\" export.\n\nThe alternative PDF format likely captures rendered versions of documents and notes, which could theoretically include more data, but PDFs are not computable and there's no documentation of what the PDF export contains.\n\n**Domains likely covered** (by virtue of C-CDA 2.1):\n- Demographics\n- Diagnoses/problems\n- Medications\n- Allergies\n- Vital signs\n- Immunizations\n- Procedures\n- Lab/diagnostic results (if applicable)\n- Encounters\n- Clinical notes (as unstructured text in C-CDA sections)\n\n**Domains likely missing or unverifiable:**\n- Billing records (claims, charges, payments, CPT codes, ERA)\n- Insurance/payer details\n- Palliative-specific clinical assessments and symptom ratings\n- IDG meeting records and documentation\n- Orders (DME, supplies)\n- Comprehensive plan of care (palliative-specific detail beyond C-CDA's generic plan of care section)\n- Advance directives (may be partially in C-CDA)\n- Physician communications\n- Emergency preparedness documentation\n- Referral tracking data\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\n- **Format**: C-CDA 2.1 XML and PDF, delivered in a ZIP archive\n- **Standard**: C-CDA (Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture) version 2.1 is a recognized HL7 standard for clinical document exchange\n- **Appropriateness**: C-CDA is appropriate for clinical summaries but is a poor fit for exporting \"all electronic health information\" from a palliative care EHR. A palliative care product stores specialty-specific data (symptom assessments, IDG records, comprehensive plans of care, billing) that doesn't map to C-CDA sections.\n- **Reconstruction**: A third party could reconstruct a basic clinical summary from the C-CDA export but almost certainly could not reconstruct the full patient record, especially billing, palliative-specific assessments, and administrative data.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\nThe documentation quality is **extremely poor**:\n- A single page with no technical depth\n- No data dictionary at all\n- No field-level definitions\n- No data types, value sets, or constraints\n- No sample exports or worked examples\n- No schema files or machine-readable specifications\n- No description of which C-CDA templates or sections are used\n- Contains an internal note (\"This should comply with what we need and buy us time to finish the feature\") that was not removed before publication\n- The documentation reads as an internal memo rather than a technical specification\n\nA developer could not implement an import of this data based on this documentation alone. They would know only that the export is \"C-CDA 2.1 XML\" in a ZIP — they'd need to reverse-engineer the actual structure from sample exports.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Granularity**: Zero field-level documentation. Not even table-level or section-level documentation.\n- **Value sets**: Not documented\n- **Relationships**: Not documented\n- **Versioning**: The PDF was created December 15, 2023. No change history.\n- **Machine-readable artifacts**: None provided\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://www.axxess.com/cehrt/\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no (all content accessible via curl)\n- Navigation complexity: one_click (PDF linked directly from CEHRT page)\n- Anti-bot issues: none\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- The FHIR API sandbox documentation (`r4dev.dynamicfhirsandbox.com`) timed out but was determined to be (g)(10) documentation, not relevant to the (b)(10) export.\n- The partner API page (`engage.axxess.com/api.html`) is a marketing/lead-gen page, not technical documentation.\n- The help center (`axxess.com/help/axxess-palliative-care/`) has ~40+ articles but none specifically about the \"Download Patient Chart\" EHI export feature.
